gen-gf-neucha-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a constant stripe of ink, while Neucha's broad-nib curves stay tight-knit and left unfinished. Friendly hand above, steady line below; not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-gf-neucha-plus-jakarta-sans: Graceful and friendly, Neucha leans on a broad-nib hand. Plus Jakarta Sans steps in with monoline, sans-serif precision and curve endings kept well apart, pleasant whenever the text stays brief.
gen-gf-neucha-sora: Loose, hand-drawn charm: Neucha keeps tight-knit words and unfinished broad-nib curves. Sora brings the precision, a geometric sans with no pressure swell at the corners, made for brief reading.
gen-gf-nova-flat-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, its thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. But Nova Flat's rounded-wire strokes carry the commanding punch, while Rowan handles the quieter, brief lines.
gen-gf-nova-oval-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve and thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones. Nova Oval adds bold expression up top, and Rowan suits brief lines.
gen-gf-offside-gf-hepta-slab: Widely tracked and restless, Offside leaves its curves open and holds a quiet, level beat. Hepta Slab, the text serif here, is the dignified backbone, open counters breathing into white space.
gen-gf-offside-gf-stint-ultra-expanded: Wide and commanding: Offside tracks its letters far apart while Stint Ultra Expanded floats each character like a pipe cleaner. A modest body size leaves its wide letters room to settle.
gen-gf-oldenburg-gf-kiwi-maru: Commanding Oldenburg draws its curves with a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look and shallow lowercase. Kiwi Maru, a traditional serif with terminals stopping far from the stem, adds the editorial counterweight.
gen-gf-overlock-fs-paquito: Overlock's s curves open wide at both ends, commanding and bold. Paquito, a text serif that barely separates x-height from caps, adds confident, approachable ease that suits brief lines.
gen-gf-pangolin-fs-hind: Pangolin looks drawn with a single nib, its tall, generous lowercase and wide apertures giving it a friendly, relaxed manner. Hind's string-like strokes carry extended text smoothly, though brief lines suit it best.
